subject: Proposal: SKU price lock & commit upgrade path
messages:
From: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@bluespruce.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Procurement <procurement@bluespruce.com>, Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@bluespruce.com>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal: pricing inquiry + SKU lock request

Karthik —

Thanks for taking this. We’re kicking off our renewal cycle for BlueSpruce and want to align on pricing before we send PO. Usage has increased ~2.6x year-over-year after the product search rollout; we’d like to lock current per-token SKU pricing for 12 months while we finalize higher commit tiers.

High level ask: can Redwood provide a temporary price hold at current rates for the next 12 months, plus a one-time credit for overage in Q2 to offset our onboarding spike? If we commit to a 30% uplift in committed capacity across alpha+beta SKUs for 18 months, we’d expect a material discount to justify the longer commitment.

I’ve attached a short usage extract and the renewal timing. Procurement is ready to raise a PO once terms are agreed.

Appreciate a quick confirmation of whether this is feasible and what the tradeoffs look like.

—Daniel
Daniel Cho
Head of Engineering, BlueSpruce Systems
attachments: BlueSpruce_Renewal_Request_20270531.pdf, BS_Renewal_TCV_breakdown.csv

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@bluespruce.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: pricing inquiry + SKU lock request

Daniel —

Thanks for the context and the data. Congrats on the rapid adoption — that growth helps us build a better case for capacity planning. Short answer: we can get close to what you’re asking, but there are tradeoffs depending on duration and commit shape.

Proposed counter (high level):
- 12-month price hold at your current per-token rates for all existing SKUs if BlueSpruce agrees to an 18-month total commitment length and a 30% uplift in committed capacity across alpha+beta SKUs.
- One-time Q2 onboarding credit equal to 10% of the incremental spend in April–May (applied as invoice credit).
- If you can accelerate 70% of the uplift in the first 6 months we can extend a 12% effective discount on committed units for months 1–12 (blend of discount + usage-based credits).

Need to confirm a couple things before I send a formal term sheet: current BLU SKU split by monthly tokens (we saw the extract but want normalized monthly cadence), and whether BlueSpruce needs invoice deferral or PO timing accommodations. Also looping in Marissa for commercial approval and Grace for CS handoff on migration/measuring uplift.

I’ll draft a formal counter with the exact billing mechanics and a sample amendment if we get the go-ahead.

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attachments: Legal_redlines_v1.docx

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: BlueSpruce — counter & approval needed

Marissa / Priyom —

BlueSpruce (DL-2027-0934) requested a 12-month price hold + onboarding credit; they’re proposing a potential 30% uplift to committed capacity and will sign for longer if we provide a price hold. I sketched the commercial counter below (same as to Daniel):
- 18-month commitment term
- 12-month price hold at current rates
- One-time credit = 10% of incremental April–May spend (applied against next invoice)
- Early uplift acceleration (70% within 6 months) triggers an extra 12% effective discount on committed units for months 1–12

Why this is reasonable: preserves short-term revenue per token while converting part of the expansion into committed revenue; the acceleration trigger protects us from immediate overcommit in case usage is backloaded.

Ask: marissa, do we have flexibility on the 12% effective discount number? Priyom, I attached a redline with the amendment language and a suggested invoice-credit mechanic — can you do a quick run to flag any legal procurement concerns (PO timing, tax/compliance on credits, wording for invoice credit)? Grace, can you confirm we can operationalize the 70% acceleration measurement?

Attachments: Legal_redlines_v1.docx, BlueSpruce_Renewal_Request_20270531.pdf

—Karthik

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: BlueSpruce — counter & approval needed

Karthik —

We can support this structure with a tweak. Commercial OK from my side if we adjust the uplift-trigger discount cadence slightly to protect margin. Proposal:
- 18-month term as proposed
- 12-month price hold at current rates
- One-time onboarding credit = 10% of incremental Apr–May spend (same)
- Acceleration trigger: if 70% of uplift is delivered in the first 6 months, apply a 8% sustained discount on committed units for months 1–12 (instead of 12%).
- In lieu of a cash credit we can offer invoice deferral (one month) to help their procurement cadence — this reduces the immediate cash impact.

If procurement needs a playbook we’ll include: amendment + SOW for uplift schedule + usage tracking dashboard. I’ve drafted a DocuSign envelope link for signature (internal only for now): https://redwood.docusign.com/envelopes/ENV-87921

Priyom — approved to run the attached redline through legal with the invoice-credit vs invoice-deferral options called out. Grace — confirm ops can measure uplift by SKU and timestamp so triggers are auditable.

—Marissa
Sr. Sales Director, Redwood Inference

From: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@bluespruce.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Procurement <procurement@bluespruce.com>, Lina Gomez <lina.gomez@bluespruce.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: pricing inquiry + SKU lock request

Karthik / Marissa —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the flexibility. BlueSpruce is comfortable with the 18-month term and the 12-month price hold. We prefer the invoice deferral option over a cash credit; procurement will raise a PO with a one-month deferral note.

Next steps from our side: procurement will send PO + W9 by EOD Friday. I’ll accept the DocuSign envelope once legal confirms redlines (looping in our counsel). Please send the final amendment and countersign path and we’ll execute.

Thanks — looking forward to locking this in.

—Daniel
Head of Engineering, BlueSpruce Systems

Thanks — I’ll route the amendment/DocuSign with Marissa’s agreed commercial terms (18m term / 12m price hold / invoice deferral option / 8% acceleration discount trigger) this morning. Priyom will handle the final legal redline and I’ll confirm an expected countersign ETA once they send the PO.

Attached: copy of the amendment we’ll push into DocuSign and a clean SOW template for the uplift schedule. Once procurement sends PO and W9 we’ll complete the countersign and flip to onboarding (Grace will coordinate).
